GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to BowlbugNectar.cs:43-56, including the detail that makes this monster odd: there are TWO distinct MoveStates sharing the ThrashMove delegate, THRASH_MOVE and THRASH2_MOVE, and the chain is THRASH -> BUFF -> THRASH2 -> THRASH2 (a self-loop), initial THRASH. So the +15 Strength lands exactly once and the bug thrashes forever afterwards. The sim reproduces both states and the self-loop, and even the registration order ([BUFF, THRASH2, THRASH]) matches. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs).

guards.rationale: BowlbugNectar.cs:29 ThrashDamage is a flat 3 with no ascension gate at all; BuffStrengthGain (:31) non-ascension is 15. Sim bowlbugs.py:30-31 = 3 / 15. BuffMove applies the Strength to itself (:69) -- sim _buff (bowlbugs.py:141-144) does the same, so THRASH2 hits for 3 + 15.
BowlbugNectar declares none (unlike its Egg and Rock siblings), so the base no-op runs and the sim's inherited MachineMonster.__init__ matches. SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 does not apply.
